shape_hint: A wire spring clip shaped like the letter R: a straight leg that is pushed through the cross-hole of a pin, and a second leg that is bent back and wound as a double (two-turn) coil eye of outer diameter d4 which snaps around the outside of the pin. Total length l1; the wire cross-section is a plain circle of diameter d3.

role_map.d1: nominal hole diameter in the pin the clip passes through (H13)
role_map.d2_min: smallest pin/shaft diameter the clip fits (exclusive)
role_map.d2_max: largest pin/shaft diameter the clip fits
role_map.d4: outer diameter of the double coil eye
role_map.l2: second length dimension on the standard drawing (about 0.55-0.6 x l1)

notes: Only DIN 11024 Form D (double coil, 'R-clip with double spring') is published. Form E (single coil) has a different series (d1=2.5..9 with l=50..110) and is NOT in this table. DIN 11023 (linch pin) was not researched. Some sellers sell 'similar to DIN 11024' clips with other wire diameters (e.g. 2.0-8.0 round sizes); do not mix. Size label = hole diameter d1 (what buyers call 'R-clip 4' / 'Ø4'). The exact geometric meaning of l2 was not stated in the HTML sources (only the symbol); treat as drawing dimension. Mass is informational and has exactly 3 sources (fixawell, voigt, kleinsorge).

verification.checks_done: Re-fetched fixawell, fasteners.eu/standards/din/11024-D, voigt, kleinsorge, industriehof, fasenco (all 200) and Aspen PDF (parsed with pymupdf). 7 rows x 7 value cols (d2_min,d2_max,d3,d4,l1,l2,kg100) x 7 sources: 0 numeric mismatches. Counted clusters per kept col (d2_min,d2_max,d3,l1): rows 2.5-7 = 4 (fe/fix, voigt+klein merged, industriehof, fasenco); row 8 = 3 (industriehof has no 8). l2: rows 2.5-7 = 3 (fe/fix, voigt+klein merged, industriehof), row 8 = 2. kg100: 2 for all rows (fe/fix, voigt+klein merged; industriehof gives only rounded per-piece weights 0.006..0.090 kg = 0.6..9.0 per 100, not equal to 0.59..9.7). Sanity: d2 ranges contiguous, d3<d1, l2<l1, all cols monotone.
problems: d4 role inferred wrongly: producer labels it 'outer diameter of the coil eye'; fasteners.eu legend says only 'diameter of the eye' and Keller&Kalmbach (item 2029563, DIN 11024 D 6.3) calls the same 25 mm 'Inner diameter di' (and wire 'Diameter d 5.6'). Inner vs outer differ by 2 x wire dia -> semantics unclear, column dropped (values themselves have >=3 clusters).

kg100 only 3 sources (fasteners.eu/fixawell, voigt, kleinsorge). voigt and kleinsorge show identical column set (d1..l2, mass/100), identical 'galv. verzinkt / vergutet' wording and Voigt's d2 '14,0 - 20' looks like a hand-trimmed copy of '14,0 - 20,0' style data; independence cannot be proven. If they merge only 2 clusters remain -> drop kg100.

l2: row 8 has only fe/fix + voigt + kleinsorge (same fragility) -> 2 clusters if merged; rows 2.5-7 would be fine (industriehof L2 equal). Column dropped for simplicity; per-cell alternative: keep l2 for rows 2.5-7 only. l2 is defined in the fasteners.eu legend ('distance of the center bolt from the eye'); producer's label '(drawing symbol)' is vague.

d2_min labelled 'exclusive (over)': industriehof shows 'ab 9,0 - 11,2' (inclusive) for d1=2.5 and 'uber ...' (exclusive) only for rows 3.2-8; contiguity 11.2/14/20/26/34/45 holds. Relabel as 'shaft diameter range lower bound'.
d1 row label = hole in the pin (industriehof 'Wellenbohrung D1'), d2 = pin diameter range ('Wellen D2'), d3 = wire (fe legend 'diameter wire'): roles confirmed by headers/legends.
Row 8 depends on fasenco being independent of the fasteners.eu family (it shares only the h column; its '9.0 - 11.2' formatting differs from fe's '9-11,2'); if merged, row 8 would fall to 2 clusters.

aspenfasteners PDF disclaims 'data obtained from publicly available sources' (corroboration only); boltsfastener 11024 pages are copies of the fasenco/aspen layout; schrauben-lexikon 'DIN 11024 D' table is a different dataset (excluded by producer, agreed).

standard_full: DIN 11024 Form D (double-coil spring cotter / R-clip)
